approachQuestion.prompt:
Exact average periods. Count nonempty contiguous intervals whose arithmetic mean is exactly the given integer v. Avoid floating-point rounding. Return a count.

Input: a=[1,3,2], v=2. Output: 3.

Constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 200000; -1000000 ≤ a[i],v ≤ 1000000. All transformed sums and counts fit signed 64 bits.

Which approach handles the complete task correctly and efficiently?

options.text: Scan transformed values a[i]-v without storing a transformed array. Maintain their running sum S and a frequency map seeded with 0:1; add frequency[S] before incrementing it.
options.feedback: An interval has mean v exactly when its sum minus its length times v is zero. Equal transformed boundary totals count precisely those intervals.

options.text: Count intervals whose untransformed total equals v.
options.feedback: For [1,3], v=2, the whole interval has mean 2 but total 4; the method misses it.

options.text: Enumerate all intervals, maintaining their sum and length, and test sum==length*v.
options.feedback: This gives correct results, but repeatedly traverses overlapping candidates. The selected summary reuses their shared work.

Subtracting v from every entry turns sum/length=v into transformed sum zero. This avoids floating average comparisons and applies to signed values. Compute the transformation while scanning instead of storing a second array.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the method in the reveal. Choose its tightest expected-time and worst-case auxiliary-space pair. Hash operations take expected constant time with amortized resizing; arithmetic on bounded 64-bit values is constant time. No transformed copy or recursive stack is allocated; include map and exclude input/scalar output.

options.text: Expected O(n) time; O(n) auxiliary space
Worst-case O(n) time; O(n) auxiliary space
Expected O(n) time; O(1) auxiliary space
Expected O(n²) time; O(1) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Transform values on arrival and count equal prefix totals.
details: Each transformation and expected constant-time map operation occurs once per element. Up to n+1 distinct transformed totals occupy O(n) space.

Hash operations take expected constant time with amortized resizing; arithmetic on bounded 64-bit values is constant time. No transformed copy or recursive stack is allocated; include map and exclude input/scalar output.

For each of n values, subtract v, update one running transformed total, then perform a bounded number of expected-amortized constant-time frequency-map operations. Total time is expected O(n). The worst-case O(n) choice is not guaranteed by non-adversarial expected hashing. The potentially quadratic answer is accumulated numerically rather than by visiting every qualifying interval.

There can be n+1 distinct transformed prefix totals, so retained frequencies require O(n) auxiliary space. No transformed input copy is allocated, but that does not make space O(1): the map remains. The quadratic/constant-space option changes both the scan's operation count and its retained state. Input and scalar output are excluded.
